games.blurb: Lure a flock of starlings through a string of gates before night falls. Startle them for speed, but panic spreads from bird to bird.
games.goal: Fly 15 birds through each of the 5 gates, in order and close together, before night falls (60 seconds of light) and before the flock drops below 15 birds.
games.howToPlay: The flock steers itself: birds stay close to their neighbors and match their heading. {Hold} anywhere and calm birds fly toward your {finger}; keep holding and move it to lead them. The dashed circle shows how far the lure reaches; it pulls hardest on birds near it, but birds that fly inside the ring around your {finger} are spooked, and the ring turns red. So keep it ahead of the flock and keep moving, rather than pressing on the birds. {Tap} to startle the birds near the {tap}: they panic (turning red) and burst away from it. Scared birds still match their neighbors' heading, so a {tap} just behind the flock sends it surging forward, the fastest way across open sky. A gate only counts birds that flew through it in the last few seconds, so bring the flock through together. The sky darkens as the light runs out (the time left is in the bottom bar); if the flock hasn't cleared all 5 gates by nightfall, the round is lost. Fear spreads to neighbors and fades over time. Scared birds ignore your lure, birds packed too tightly get scared on their own, and panicked birds can fly off the edge of the sky and be lost, so be careful startling near the edges.

games.blurb: Draw scent trails to lead your ants to food over six days. The colony carries over, and every day brings something new: scattered food, storms, a second spider, a rival colony.
games.goal: Survive a six-day run. Each day, carry the day's crumbs into the nest before sundown (60 seconds on day 1, then 90) without the colony dropping below 8 ants. Ants alive at sundown start the next day.
games.howToPlay: Ants wander until they smell something. Drag to draw a scent trail (it uses up the scent meter, which refills). Ants follow trails away from the nest, grab a crumb, and walk straight home, laying scent as they go, so busy routes grow into bright highways. Scent fades over time. Spiders follow scent too, and move fastest on the strongest trails. {Press} and hold to make it rain: rain washes scent away, so you can throw a spider off a trail, but your ants lose that trail as well. Soldiers keep spiders away from the nest, and a new ant hatches for every 10 crumbs. Day 1 is a short warm-up with one pile and no spider. Every day after it has a new food layout and a twist: day 4 brings storm clouds that wash trails as they drift by, day 5 a second spider, day 6 a rival colony of red ants that raids the same food and follows your trails. Ants you lose stay lost, but overnight one ant hatches for every 10 seconds of daylight you had left, plus 3 more if you met the day's bonus challenge (bottom left). Lose a day and you can retry it with the ants you had at dawn, or start a new run. The ▶▶ button (bottom right) runs the day at 2× or 3× speed.

games.blurb: Heat an iron bar and hammer it into shape: heat decides where the metal goes.
games.goal: Hammer the bar until every segment matches the dashed outline. Three cracks, or running out of fuel with nothing left hot enough to work, ends the round.
games.howToPlay: {Hold} anywhere above or below the bar to heat the part under your {finger} ({slide} to move the heat); it burns fuel from the gauge at the top. Heat spreads along the bar and always fades, and thin metal heats and cools faster. {Tap} to strike a segment once a small hammer mark shows above it. Temperature shows as colour: black iron is too cold to move (the hammer just bounces off), and striking dull red (a grey crack mark, no hammer yet) cracks the bar; from bright cherry through orange and yellow each blow thins the segment, hotter blows thin it more; white-hot metal (a flame over the hammer) burns away. The metal you knock out of a segment flows into its neighbours, mostly into the hotter one: a cold neighbour takes almost nothing. So to thicken a segment, get it hotter than the segment on the other side and strike the segment next to it. Arrows under a hot segment show where its metal will go if you strike it now. A green dot under a segment means it matches the outline. The legend at the bottom shows the working range. There is no clock: take your time, but fuel spent on metal that cools off is wasted.

games.keyboard: Arrows pick a meadow · Enter/Space release rabbits · F then an arrow picks a path, F fences/unfences it · N next season
games.blurb: Keep rabbits and foxes in balance on a small island for two years, one season at a time.
games.goal: Get through 8 seasons (two years) with both rabbits and foxes alive. Every season that ends with either species outside its band on the census meters is a strike; three strikes, or either species dying out, ends the round.
games.howToPlay: The island is a set of meadows joined by paths. Each season you get 2 moves, then {press} Next season to watch it play out. {Tap} a meadow to release 8 rabbits there. Drag across a path to put up a fence: foxes can't cross it, but rabbits slip under it. You can have 3 fences up at once, and dragging across a fence takes it down for free. Rabbits eat grass (meadows go dark and lose their tufts when grazed bare), breed fastest in spring and not at all in winter, and move away from foxes and crowding. Foxes eat rabbits, raise cubs when well fed, starve when not, and follow the rabbits: the orange arrows on the paths show where they're heading next. Numbers under each meadow are its rabbits (after a dot) and foxes (after a triangle). The meters at the top show both totals against their band (a number outside it says low or high). Protect rabbits too well and the foxes starve; leave the foxes free and they eat the island bare. The second year brings one surprise, announced a season ahead.

games.title: Loom
games.blurb: Stretch a knotted net onto a dotted silhouette and pin it there before the pins pop or the strands snap.
games.goal: Hold seven shapes in a row: cover every dot with a knot at once and keep it there for a second. Three slips (a pin popping loose or a strand snapping) lose the shape (one frayed strand snapping loses it at once), and snapped strands stay snapped for the rest of the run.
games.howToPlay: Drag a knot to pull the net: the knot follows your {finger}, and the further your {finger} leads it, the harder you pull. {Tap} a knot to pin it where it is (up to 4 pins); {tap} a pin to take it out, or drag it to pull it out and move that knot. A knot you let go of without a pin slides back as the net relaxes, so pin it quickly. Strands turn from linen to gold as they stretch, then darker and thicker orange to red near their limit; a strand crossed by two white bars is over it and snaps if it stays there. The ring around a pin fills with the load it holds; it turns thick and red when the pin is close to giving, and an outer white ring means it is working loose and about to pop. While you pull, the same ring around your knot shows the load a pin would hold if you pinned it there. A dot only needs a knot somewhere inside its circle, so the near edge needs less stretch than the middle. A taut edge between two pins lines up the knots along it, which can cover extra dots without extra pins. Later shapes add twists: a blue dot only counts under the blue knot, and dashed frayed strands tear at a third of the usual stretch, so keep them slack. Shapes are mirrored at random each run.

Pulling writes it around the dragged knot; pins fix knots so tension builds between them, and each pin reads the tension of its strands (too much and it pops, releasing its knot and passing the load on). A strand past its limit snaps for good. Where the knots end up, which the silhouette reads, is set by that tension balance.

games.blurb: Tilt a terraced hillside to slosh water where each plant wants it, and open the gates to let it down the slope.
games.goal: Make every plant bloom in a short warm-up and then three gardens in a row, before the spring's water runs out. Each plant needs its own depth of water. Water that spills off the bottom terrace, leaks away or is drunk never comes back.
games.howToPlay: {Tap} the spring's valve at the top to let water out, and {tap} a gate at the end of a terrace to open or close it: an open gate lets water down to the terrace below. Tilt to slosh all the water at once: toward the gates to send it down, away to hold it back, or to pile it up at one end. On a phone, tilt the phone (however you hold it when a garden starts counts as level), or {slide} the bar under the hillside if tilt is off (on a computer, drag the bar or use the keys). Each plant has a stake with a green band: it grows while the water over it is inside the band, and drinks as it grows. Too shallow and it waits, too deep and it bubbles. An open gate still keeps a shallow puddle behind it, which only a tilt will bring down. There's no clock: take your time. If the hillside goes still, an arrow or a pulsing gate shows a move that helps. Spring water left over when a garden blooms carries on to the next one.
games.keyboard: ← → or A / D tilt · ↑ ↓ pick a gate, Enter or G opens or shuts it · 0–4 that gate (0 spring) · S status

games.blurb: Turn a sealed box of sand to float its air bubbles out through the vent. Sand falls, bubbles rise, and glass you melt from the sand holds it back. Three chapters, timed.
games.goal: Free the bubbles through the gold vent in twenty-one boxes, over three chapters. There's no clock on a box and no way to lose: if one gets hopelessly stuck, restart it. Your score is the time a whole chapter takes, played in order from its first box, restarts included.
games.howToPlay: Drag around the box to turn it (on a phone you can also switch Tilt on and turn the phone itself). Gravity turns with it: sand always falls and the bubble always rises, so one turn moves both, in opposite directions. Sand trickles past the bubble in open water, slower the deeper it is, but in a narrow tube the bubble fills, sand stops it: its outline turns red. From level 2, {hold} on sand to melt it into glass. The glass grows toward your {finger} while you {hold}, costs heat, and is solid: it falls as one piece and blocks sand and the bubble, so it can make a lid, a roof or a plug. From level 3, {tap} glass to shatter it back into sand where it is. That's free, but the sand falls wherever gravity says. If that sand would bury a bubble, or the glass is a lid, the first {tap} only warns: {tap} again to break it. Some levels point at where to melt from the start. Chapter 2 brings dark wet sand (heavy: a thin layer stops the bubble, it falls slowly and won't melt), pale dust (light and fast) and grey grates that sand falls through but the bubble can't. Chapter 3 has two bubbles: both must get out, and bubbles that touch join into one that is too big for narrow tubes. If nothing moves for a few seconds, a hint shows a turn, a place to melt, glass to shatter, or Restart.

games.title: Tidewright
games.blurb: Flick sand onto a seawall and work the sluice gates to keep the village dry, wave after wave.
games.goal: Keep the water behind the wall below the flood line for as many waves as you can. Every 6 waves a season is won and the wall carries over.
games.howToPlay: You look out from the village at your sand wall, with the sea behind it. The white line shows how high the next wave will reach; the timer says when. Flick (a quick {swipe}) anywhere above a column to throw sand onto it: a faster {swipe} throws more, and a sideways {swipe} spreads it that way. Sand comes from a pile that refills slowly. Water that gets over or through the wall pools at its foot and softens it, and sand thrown into standing water mostly washes away. {Tap} a gate handle to open that sluice: it drains the pooled water out while the sea is low, but lets the sea pour in when a wave comes or on a spring tide, when the blue sea line stands above the gates. Drain in the calm, shut before the crest, build on dry sand. From wave 3 the sea seeps through the wall; later waves bring rogue waves, rain, spring tides, double waves and storms.
games.keyboard: ← → pick a column, hold and release Space to throw sand (longer = more), 1-4 open or shut a gate

mechanics.description: {Tap} a gate handle to open or shut it. Open gates drain the water behind the wall down to the sill, or let the sea in when it stands higher.

games.title: Rail Sorting Yard
games.blurb: A turn-based shunting puzzle: set switches and flick cars down the tracks to build the outbound train in order. Cars couple only at the right speed, and gravel, full sidings and one-way gates get in the way.
games.goal: Build the outbound train on the gold departure track, in the order shown at the top (buffer end first), in ten yards over two chapters. Nothing moves until you flick and there is no clock. Each yard has a par, the fewest flicks that can do it: your score is 100 points per yard at par, 10 fewer per extra move, summed over the run.
games.howToPlay: Drag a car along its track and let go to flick it: the farther you drag, the faster it rolls (speed 1 to 15, shown while you aim). Every car length of plain track costs 1 speed; gravel (brown, double ticks) costs 2. A rolling car that meets another at impact 2 to 4 couples to it; slower only touches, faster bounces back. A flick moves the car and everything coupled in front of it, and lets go of the cars behind. A switch sends a car rolling in from its point end down one track or the other: drag its lever toward a track, or {tap} it. Switch changes are free; only flicks count as moves. Sidings hold as many cars as their label says. Chapter 2 adds tank cars, whose round couplers repel the square ones on box cars and hoppers (the flat car’s double coupler takes both), blue one-way gates, and amber 1× gates that drop for good once the cars that used them clear the gateway. Undo is unlimited, but the undone flick still counts; a hint shows the next move for +2 moves; Restart is always there.
games.keyboard: Space picks a car (Shift+Space back) · 1–9, + − speed · arrows flick · A–D switches · Z undo · H hint · X restart

games.sharedState: Each rolling car’s speed. The flick sets it; the route the switches pick decides how fast it drains (plain track 1 per car length, gravel 2); what is left when it meets a car or buffer decides the outcome: couple (2 to 4), touch (0 to 1) or bounce back (5 and up).

games.blurb: Turn a sealed glass vessel all the way round so its water floats a glowing bead to the exit ring.
games.goal: Carry the bead into the gold ring on each level. Cups lock the ring: it opens only while every cup holds water in its green band. Score more for pearls, bullseye levels and water brought home.
games.howToPlay: {Press} anywhere and turn your {finger} around the vessel like a dial to rotate it; gravity stays down, so the water pours and the bead floats along on it. On a phone you can also turn on Tilt and turn the phone itself: the vessel stays level on the screen and the water falls to the real down. {Tap} Tilt again, or drag the vessel, to switch back. A cup fills only when you turn its mouth upward; {tap} its valve button below to shut it and keep the water while you turn back. When every cup sits in its green band the ring opens: float the bead in. Turning is free and there is no clock. Points: clearing the level, each pink pearl the bead touches, each cup level on its dotted centre line, and how much water ends up in the ring's chamber (on colour levels, each colour in its own chamber). Colour levels: a cup counts only its own colour and may hold at most 20% of the other; colours never separate once mixed, so use ↻ to start again.

games.blurb: One coin is fake. Weigh, mark what you learn, and prove which one before the weighings run out.
games.goal: Crack as many cases as you can in one run. A case is cracked when you accuse the fake and the weighings prove it; a wrong coin, a lucky guess or running out of weighings is a strike (the first loss on each of the 12 campaign cases is a free retry). Three strikes end the run.
games.howToPlay: {Swipe} coins from the tray onto the pans, then {hold} the beam (or press Weigh) to spend a weighing. The heavier pan tips down and the coins stay put so you can read the result; every weighing spends one of the dots at the top. {Tap} a coin to mark what you know about it: ? unknown, H could be heavy, L could be light, ✓ genuine. The game never fills marks in, and the log only keeps counts, so your marks are your memory. When you are sure, {tap} Accuse and {tap} the fake (two coins when there are two fakes). New rules arrive case by case: fakes that may be lighter, pans that hold only a few coins, two fakes, and a spring scale that shows grams (genuine 10 g, fake ±1 g) instead of tipping. Hint (once per case) shows the counts for the best next weighing.
games.keyboard: Arrows or 1-9 pick a coin, L / R load it, T back to tray, M mark, Space weigh, A accuse, H hint, Esc clear

games.blurb: Hang each coat behind an identical door, then find it again from one word on a ticket. Where you hang it is all you have.
games.goal: Return as many coats as you can in one run. A shift is cleared when every guest has their coat back; three complaints (wrong doors) lose it. The first loss on each of the 12 campaign shifts is a free retry with new coats; after that, Endless runs until a shift is lost.
games.howToPlay: Guests hand over coats one at a time. Drag the coat from the counter onto any free hook and its door shuts: closed doors all look the same, and nothing on screen lists what went where. Later a guest shows a ticket naming one thing about their coat (its colour, its pattern or its pin); {tap} the door you think hides it. A wrong door shows you what is there and the guest complains. {Hold} a door until the ring around your {finger} closes to peek behind it without opening it for the guest; peeks are limited (the dots in the bar). Each shift adds a rule: look-alike coats, a coach party of one colour, a manager who reorders a row, friends whose ticket names the coat handed in just before theirs, two-feature tickets, and regulars whose coats stay overnight. After each shift every door opens for a moment so you can see your own system.

games.title: Mycelium
games.blurb: Grow a fungal network through the soil to reach food, keep its far threads fed, and fruit mushrooms before the frost.
games.goal: Grow each season's mushrooms before the frost. Your nutrient pool carries over; after 8 seasons the seasons keep coming, leaner each time. Score: mushrooms over the run.
games.howToPlay: The glowing spore in the middle is your network's heart. Drag from it (or from any knot of your network) to a leaf patch to grow a thread there; each new knot costs nutrient from your pool, and every knot costs a little upkeep each second (shown next to the pool). A patch your thread reaches feeds the pool until it is used up. {Tap} a knot to pulse: a surge of nutrient leaves the pool and runs out along the thread, refilling every knot on the way; what reaches a patch grows a mushroom there, and what reaches any other knot is spilled. Knots more than 3 threads from the spore or a feeding patch slowly fade: pulse them, or they starve, and a thread that starves while attached rots back toward the spore. {Hold} a knot to cut the thread into it: everything beyond withers harmlessly and stops costing upkeep, and growing into it again reconnects it. When the pool is empty the network eats its own farthest tips. Later seasons bring an old log far out, dry soil (4× upkeep), rival moulds racing you to food ({hold} a rival knot to cut it), stones and patches that fall mid-season; from season 5 every knot costs more upkeep, so cut what no longer feeds you.

mechanics.description: {Hold} a knot to cut the thread into it: the branch beyond withers without rotting and stops costing upkeep. Also cuts rival mould.

Pulses refill sap along a thread; knots too far from a feeding patch lose sap and, starving, rot back. Cutting stops a branch's upkeep and its rot.

games.title: Lighthouse Keeper
games.blurb: Turn the lighthouse beam through the fog so ships can see the rocks, and ration the oil to last the night.
games.goal: Bring each night's ships into the harbour with no more than 2 wrecks. Oil carries over; after 8 nights the nights keep coming, foggier and busier. Score: ships brought home over the run.
games.howToPlay: Ships sail out of the dark toward the harbour (bottom left). In thick fog a ship can't see and holds its course, drifting, straight onto any rocks in its way; its mast light flashes red. Drag across the sea to turn the beam: it burns the fog away where it points, and a ship it lights (green mast light) sees the rocks and steers home around them. The fog drifts back within seconds once the beam moves on. The open lamp burns oil, and every ship that docks brings a little more. {Tap} the lighthouse to shutter the lamp (no oil burns, but the sea goes dark) and {tap} it again to open it. {Hold} the lighthouse to charge a flare and let go to fire it where the beam points: it clears a wide patch of fog for several seconds, and a bigger flare costs more oil. A third wreck loses the night. Later nights bring drifting fog banks, ships from the right, heavy ships that turn slowly, convoys and storms.

games.title: Surprise Party
games.blurb: Spread the word about the party through the house as a ripple of whispers, and steer it with doors so the birthday person doesn't hear before 8:00.
games.goal: Get every guest in each house to hear about the party by 8:00 while the birthday person hears nothing before then. 15 houses in three chapters (stars for envelopes saved), then Party Season: endless new houses, envelopes carry over, and the score is the parties you pull off before they run out.
games.howToPlay: It's 6:00 and the party starts at 8:00; every move takes 15 minutes. {Tap} a guest to whisper the news (it costs one envelope). Anyone who just heard tells everyone within 2 steps on the next quarter hour, then goes quiet and puts on a party hat, so the news moves as a ripple and never comes back. Walls and shut doors stop it. {Hold} a door to shut or open it, or press Wait to let the clock move on. Dashed rings show who hears next; the pink tint is the birthday person's 2-step danger zone. News that reaches them exactly at 8:00 is fine: that's the surprise. Undo is free in the campaign; in Party Season an undone whisper stays spent.
games.keyboard: Arrows move · Enter whispers, next house · hold O: door · G guest, D door, B birthday · Space wait · U undo · R restart

mechanics.name: whisper
mechanics.description: {Tap} a guest who hasn't heard to tell them. Spends an envelope and starts a ripple from them on the next quarter hour.

mechanics.name: door
mechanics.description: {Hold} a door until the ring closes to shut or open it. Shut doors stop the ripple; every toggle takes 15 minutes.

games.sharedState: Who knows (not yet, just heard, quiet) and which doors are shut, against the clock. Whisper writes who knows; the spread reads who just heard and the doors to decide who hears next; Door rewrites the walking distances the spread reads, so a door shut as a ripple passes saves a whisper, and one shut too early cuts the house in two.

games.title: Geode
games.blurb: Grow a crystal that rings like a bell: seed, warm and chip away the flaws before they crack it.
games.goal: Grow each crystal to its quota and harvest it, as big and as clear as you dare, before its pool runs dry. Flaws spread by themselves; a crack that reaches the core shatters the crystal and you lose what was unbanked. Three lost geodes end the run.
games.howToPlay: {Tap} beside the crystal to place an ion where you want it. Drag the thermostat under the pool: cold grows fast but strains the crystal, the middle glow heals strain without growing much, and too hot melts your corners. The ring on the thermostat is the real temperature; it follows your setting slowly. Strain shows as amber and red, thick outlines and cross-hatching, and it spreads to neighbours; at full strain an ion cracks and shocks the ones around it. Dark foreign ions swap into the crystal and creep toward bursting (watch the arc around them): {hold} on one to snap it out, and the gap heals cleanly. Harvest once the bar reaches the quota: a bigger, clearer crystal is worth more carats, but the pool ages, impurities come faster and the ring around the pool drains. Later geodes bring cold snaps, heat waves and salt flushes. Listen: a clear crystal sounds like a chord, strain sounds out of tune (sound is optional).
games.keyboard: ← → temperature · T switches arrows to a cursor · S/Enter seed · hold C cleave · I foreign ion · H harvest · M sound

mechanics.name: seed
mechanics.description: {Tap} beside the crystal to place an ion on the nearest open site. Seeds cost more of the pool than natural growth but add no growth strain, so they fill gaps cleanly.

mechanics.name: warm
mechanics.description: Drag the thermostat: cold grows fast and strains the crystal, the glow anneals strain away, too hot melts the tips. The pool follows slowly.

mechanics.name: cleave
mechanics.description: {Hold} on an ion to snap it off, with whatever hangs from it. Clears foreign ions and relieves the strain around them.

games.sharedState: Strain per site, pool saturation and temperature. Growth (natural and seeded) writes strain and spends the pool; strain spreads to neighbours. Temperature sets how fast the pool is spent and anneals or melts by strain. Seeds read the neighbours' strain (a new ion inherits it); cleave reads it to pick what is worth the mass, and clears it.

changes.text: No balance change. Seed and cleave from the keyboard: T switches the arrows to a cursor on the crystal, S or Enter seeds there, hold C cleaves. Larger labels, a screen-reader line that says what changed, and reduced motion now stills the shimmer, pulses and drifting motes.
No gameplay change. Screen readers now get a description of the game and its controls, worded for your device.
New game: grow a crystal in a cooling pool, anneal its strain, cleave out foreign ions and harvest it before the pool runs dry.
